summary.name: YunoHost
summary.one_liner: YunoHost is a server operating system that installs on your own server so you can install and maintain self-hosted apps such as mail, calendars, file sharing, and websites with little technical knowledge.
keywords: garden your own piece of the internet
use_cases: host a website for a small organization
summary.what_it_does: YunoHost installs itself on a server and lets you install and maintain digital services (apps) that you control. The page lists example uses including calendar and contact sync, password and note storage, mailboxes, photo and music organization, websites, shared file storage (e.g. Nextcloud), real-time document editing, accounting, and team chat. It guides setup of the first admin, domain name, and internet router, and mentions setting up backups and applications. The page suggests hardware options: an ARM board or Raspberry Pi, an old tower or portable machine, or an online server (VPS).
notable: Installs on your own hardware or a VPS and manages apps through a guided setup
Non-profit, volunteer-developed project advocating decentralized, interoperable, privacy-respecting Internet
Listed on awesome-selfhosted under Self-hosting Solutions with AGPL-3.0 license, Python/Shell
caveats: Requires managing a server yourself, which the page says to weigh carefully against pros and cons
Requires a domain name and router configuration as part of setup
